| unit              | = minutes since 1992-08-31 0:00:00 |
| quantity          | = wx                               |
| unit              | = ms-1                             |
| quantity          | = wy                               |
| unit              | = ms-1                             |
| 0.0               | 10. 27                             |
| 1000              | 10 22                              |
| 2000              | 10 15                              |
| 3000              | 10 12                              |
| 1e10              | 10. 27                             |

## C.6 The external forcings file

Two definition files for the external forcings are supported, each with their own format.

### Warning:

- ◇ An important change is ongoing where only the INI-based version of the `<*.ext>` file will remain as the central place for all forcings and spatial fields.  
  See Section C.6.1 below for a full description of the migration.

### C.6.1 Migration to one external forcings format, deprecation of old format

Historically, external forcings and spatial initial fields were configured using three separate files referenced from the MDU-file:

- ◇ `ExtForceFile`: legacy external forcings file format (see Section C.6.2).
- ◇ `ExtForceFileNew`: new INI-based external forcings file format (see Section C.6.3).
- ◇ `IniFieldFile`: INI-based file containing initial fields and spatially varying parameters (see Section C.16.3).

As part of an ongoing simplification of the model schematization, all functionality currently available through the old `ExtForceFile` is now available via the new `ExtForceFileNew` (for most quantities) and the `StructureFile` (for some legacy hydraulic structures).

Additionally, all functionality currently available through the `IniFieldFile` has also been incorporated into the new INI-based external forcings file. Ultimately, a single external forcings file format will remain.

### C.6.1.1 Migration steps across upcoming releases

The transition is performed in multiple releases to allow existing models to be migrated gradually.

#### Release 2027.01

- ◇ `ExtForceFile` is *deprecated*. Existing models remain supported, but users are advised to migrate their entire old `<*.ext>` file to the INI-based format. More information can be found in Section C.6.1.2.
- ◇ `IniFieldFile` is *deprecated*. Initial fields and spatial parameter definitions should be migrated to the new external forcings file. Blocks and several keywords have been renamed and are now deprecated. More information can be found in Section C.6.1.4.
- ◇ `ExtForceFileNew` remains the recommended and fully supported keyword. Yet, the `[Meteo]` blocks are now deprecated and need to be changed into `[Spatial]` blocks. As part of this change, some meteo keywords have been renamed and the old names are deprecated. More information can be found in Section C.6.1.3.

#### Release 2027.02

- ◇ `ExtForceFile` MDU keyword remains supported, but its meaning changes. It now expects the new INI-based external forcings format. Supplying a legacy-format external forcings file will result in an error.
- ◇ `IniFieldFile` becomes *obsolete* and is no longer processed. All information previously stored in this file must be defined in the external forcings file.
- ◇ `ExtForceFileNew` MDU keyword is *deprecated*. Users should rename the MDU keyword to `ExtForceFile`.

**Future release**

- ◇ ExtForceFileNew becomes *obsolete* and is removed.
- ◇ ExtForceFile remains the only supported keyword for external forcings.
- ◇ The INI-based external forcings file becomes the single file for external forcings, initial fields and spatial parameter definitions.

**Warning:**

- ◇ Users are strongly encouraged to migrate to the INI-based external forcings format as early as possible. Models that still rely on the legacy external forcings format or on a separate IniFieldFile will require modifications before support for these workflows is removed.

**C.6.1.2 Migration of old `<*.ext>` files**Migration of a legacy external forcings file consists of moving each quantity to its appropriate successor file format. In most cases, quantities remain available and only their location within the model schematization changes. Some quantity names have been renamed to follow the newer naming conventions; these changes are documented in the corresponding sections.

The old external forcings quantities can be grouped into the following categories:

- ◇ **Boundary conditions** such as `waterlevelbnd`, `dischargebnd`, `tracerbnd` and other boundary quantities must be migrated to the new external forcings file using one or more `[Boundary]` blocks. See Section C.6.3.1.
- ◇ **Lateral discharge** quantities (`lateraldischarge`, `lateraldischargeld`, `lateraldischarge2d`) must be migrated to `[Lateral]` blocks in the new external forcings file. Instead of a single polyline filename, a location (file) and timeseries file should be given. See Section C.6.3.2.
- ◇ **Source and sink** quantities (formerly represented by `discharge_salinity_` ← `temperature_sorsin`) must be migrated to one or more `[SourceSink]` blocks in the new external forcings file. Instead of a single polyline filename, a location (file) and one or more timeseries files should be given. See Section C.6.3.5.
- ◇ **Hydraulic structure** quantities such as `pump`, `damlevel`, `gateloweredgelevel` and `generalstructure` are no longer defined through external forcings. These quantities must be migrated to the structure definition file using `[Structure]` blocks. See Appendix C.13.
- ◇ **Meteorological and other spatially varying forcing quantities** such as wind, atmospheric pressure, rainfall, heat-flux related quantities and similar spatial forcings must be migrated to the new external forcings file. In release 2027.01 these quantities are preferably defined using `[Spatial]` blocks instead of the deprecated `[Meteo]` blocks. See also Section C.6.1.3.
- ◇ **Initial condition quantities** such as `initialwaterlevel`, `initialsalinity`, `initialverticaltemperatureprofile`, and related quantities, which were historically available through the old external forcings file and later through the IniFieldFile, must be migrated to the new external forcings file. See also Section C.6.1.4.
- ◇ **Spatial parameter quantities** such as `frictioncoefficient`, `horizontaleddy` ← `viscositycoefficient`, `wave-related parameters` and other spatial model parameters must also be migrated to the new external forcings file. See also Section C.6.1.4.

Table C.4 summarizes the individual legacy `<*.ext>` keywords and their new name.

Table C.5 summarizes the legacy METHOD numeric values and their new interpolationMethod descriptive enumeration values.

Table C.6 summarizes the legacy LAYER numeric values and their new targetLayer descriptive enumeration values.

**Table C.4:** Mapping of legacy <\*.ext> keywords to [Spatial] keywords.

| Legacy keyword       | New [Spatial] keyword      |
|----------------------|----------------------------|
| QUANTITY             | quantity                   |
| FILENAME             | dataFile                   |
| VARNAME              | dataVariableFile           |
| FILETYPE             | dataFileType               |
| METHOD               | interpolationMethod        |
| EXTRAPOLATION_METHOD | extrapolationAllowed       |
| OPERAND              | operand                    |
| VALUE                | dataValue                  |
| LAYER                | targetLayer                |
| MAXSEARCHRADIUS      | extrapolationSearchRadius  |
| EXTRAPOLTOL          | Option no longer supported |

**Table C.5:** Mapping of legacy <\*.ext> METHOD values to interpolationMethod values.

| Legacy value | New interpolationMethod value                                          |
|--------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 1, 2 and 3   | linearSpaceTime                                                        |
| 4            | constant, combined with a targetMaskFile                               |
| 5            | triangulation for sample files, or bilinear for gridded ArcInfo files. |
| 6            | averaging                                                              |

**Table C.6:** Mapping of legacy <\*.ext> LAYER values to targetLayer values.

| Legacy value   | New targetLayer value      |
|----------------|----------------------------|
| -1             | bottom                     |
| 0              | all                        |
| 1, 2, ..., kmx | 1, 2, ..., kmx (unchanged) |

A complete mapping of legacy quantity names to their successor file, block type and quantity name is provided in Table C.17. Users are encouraged to consult that table when converting existing schematizations.

### C.6.1.3 Migration of Meteo blocks in new <\*.ext> files

Prior to release 2027.01, spatially varying meteorological forcings in the new external forcings file were typically defined using [Meteo] blocks. Starting from release 2027.01, the [Meteo] block is deprecated and users are encouraged to migrate all such definitions to the more generic [Spatial] block.

The migration is largely mechanical and consists of a number of straightforward renamings.

#### Block name

Replace [Meteo] by [Spatial].

## Keyword renaming

Several keywords have been renamed for consistency with other spatial field definitions. The replacements listed in Table C.7 should be applied.

**Table C.7: Mapping of [Meteo] keywords to [Spatial] keywords.**

| Deprecated keyword  | New [Spatial] keyword |
|---------------------|-----------------------|
| forcingFile         | dataFile              |
| forcingVariableName | dataVariableName      |
| value               | dataValue             |

All other settings, such as quantity, targetMaskFile, interpolationMethod and targetMaskInvert, can generally be copied unchanged.

## Operand renaming

The old notation used single-character operand values. These values should be replaced by the corresponding descriptive enumeration values in Table C.8.

**Table C.8: Mapping of operand single character values to enumeration values.**

| Old value | New value         |
|-----------|-------------------|
| O         | override          |
| A         | overrideIfMissing |
| +         | add               |
| *         | multiply          |
| N         | minimum           |
| X         | maximum           |
| V         | override          |

## Example conversion

The following example illustrates a typical migration.

Deprecated format in new <\*.ext>:

```
[Meteo]
quantity      = windx
forcingFile   = wind.nc
operand      = O
```

New format in new <\*.ext>:

```
[Spatial]
quantity      = windx
dataFile      = wind.nc
operand      = override
```

## Migration of special factor quantities

Some quantities contain the factor suffix, specifically windspeedfactor or solarradiation  $\leftrightarrow$  factor. Historically these quantities were introduced because the [Meteo] block only supported time-varying forcing data. As a result, a separate quantity name had to be introduced for a time-independent scaling factor.

The new `[Spatial]` block supports both time-dependent and time-independent spatial data. Consequently, these special factor quantities are no longer required. Instead, the original meteorological quantity can be used directly together with `operand` multiply.

The time-independent data can be spatially varying, for example in a sample file (see [Appendix C.3](#)). Alternatively, it can be constant in space too. This data value was originally supplied via the `value` keyword, which has now been renamed to `dataValue`.

For example, instead of:

```
[Meteo]
quantity      = windxy
forcingFile   = wind.nc
operand      = 0
```

and

```
[Parameter]
quantity                                 = windspeedfactor
dataFileName                               = windfarm.pol
dataFileType                                = polygon
interpolationMethod                        = constant
value                                       = 0.8
operand                                   = 0
```

the recommended approach is:

```
[Spatial]
quantity                                 = windxy
dataFile                                 = wind.nc
operand                                 = override[Spatial]
quantity                                = windxy
targetMaskFile                           = windfarm.pol
dataValue                               = 0.8
operand                                = multiply
```

In this example, all wind velocities inside the area defined by `windfarm.pol` are multiplied by a factor of 0.8.

Note that this effectively makes the original `dataFileType` = `polygon` no longer needed because a polygon mask has its own keyword `targetMaskFile`.

#### C.6.1.4 Migration of blocks in `IniFieldFile`

The functionality previously provided through the `IniFieldFile` is now available in the external forcings file using `[Spatial]` blocks. Migration is generally straightforward: most quantities retain their meaning, while only the surrounding block type and several keyword names have changed.

##### Block name

Replace both `[Parameter]` and `[Initial]` by `[Spatial]`.

##### Keyword renaming

The following keyword replacements should be applied during migration:

**Table C.9:** Mapping of IniFieldFile keywords to [Spatial] keywords.

| IniFieldFile keyword | New [Spatial] keyword |
|----------------------|-----------------------|
| value                | dataValue             |
| extrapolationMethod  | extrapolationAllowed  |

## Operand renaming

The operand syntax is identical to the migration described in Section C.6.1.3 for [Meteo]. Legacy single-character operand values should be replaced by the corresponding enumeration values. See the operand mapping in Table C.8.

## Example conversion

A typical initial field and parameter file block:

```
[Parameter]
quantity                    = frictionCoefficient
value                      = 0.025
operand                    = 0
extrapolationMethod       = 1
```

should be migrated to:

```
[Spatial]
quantity                    = frictionCoefficient
dataValue                   = 0.025
operand                    = override
extrapolationAllowed      = yes
```

## Quantity names

Some quantity names have been renamed to follow the newer naming conventions used throughout the external forcings format. The complete mapping of old and new quantity names is provided in Table C.17.

Users are encouraged to migrate to the new format as early as possible. From release 2027.02 onward, the IniFieldFile keyword becomes obsolete and all initial fields and spatial parameter definitions must be provided through the external forcings file.

### C.6.1.5 Automated migration tools

For most schematizations, manual migration is not required. Two software tools are available to assist with the conversion of existing models to the new external forcings format. The two following sections describe these tools.

#### C.6.1.5.1 Graphical User Interface

The graphical user interface fully supports the legacy external forcings format, and IniFieldFile input. Existing models can therefore be opened and edited without first performing a manual migration.

When a schematization is subsequently saved, the graphical user interface automatically writes the data using the new file formats. This includes the conversion of deprecated external forcings definitions into the corresponding new-style [Boundary], [Lateral], [SourceSink] and [Spatial] blocks, as well as the migration of data previously stored in the IniFieldFile.

### C.6.1.5.2 HYDROLIB-core conversion utility

Users who wish to migrate large numbers of schematizations, or who prefer an automated scripting workflow, can use the dedicated `extforce-convert` utility that is distributed as part of the HYDROLIB-core Python toolbox.

This utility performs batch conversion of legacy external forcing files and generates the corresponding new-format external forcings definitions. The tool is particularly useful when migrating collections of models or when integrating migration steps into automated model preparation workflows.

Further information, usage examples and installation instructions can be found in the HYDROLIB-core documentation.

#### Remarks:

- ◇ Although the automated migration tools handle the vast majority of conversion steps, users are advised to inspect the generated files and verify that the migrated schematization produces the expected results.
- ◇ Particular attention should be paid to deprecated quantities, hydraulic structure definitions, and workflows that rely on the interaction of multiple spatial forcing fields through operands.

### C.6.2 Old style external forcings

#### Warning:

- ◇ Deprecated: the old style `<*.ext>` file is now deprecated. This will become obsolete in an upcoming release and the documentation below is only kept for migration purposes. See [Section C.6.1](#) for a full description of the migration.

The name of the file is specified in the MDU-file as `ExtForceFile`. External forcings are specified in blocks key-value pairs, e.g.

```
* comments
* commentsQUANTITY =waterlevelbnd
FILENAME =tfl_01.pli
FILETYPE =9
METHOD   =3
OPERAND   =0QUANTITY = ...
FILENAME = ...
...
```

The format is not case-sensitive, but key-value pairs are expected in the *particular order*

The majority of the keywords speak for themselves or are optional. The `operand` needs some explanation. This keyword determines the operation to be performed with a new connected forcing for a quantity already set by another forcing from a different source: 'O' to replace the existing value with the new one and '+' to add the new to the existing value. Though generally applicable to all external forcings, it is most commonly used when working with spatial fields (such as wind and atmospheric pressure) originating from different types of sources. For instance a spatially uniform wind field could be set as a timeseries, but overwritten locally by a values interpolated from regional atmospheric model output, upon which a cyclone is superimposed from a spiderweb-type file. This means that the `<ext>`-file likely has three entries for quantity wind in the aforementioned order: a uniform timeseries with an operand 'O', a netCDF file with operand 'O' and a spiderweb file with operand '+'. The netCDF file might not cover the entire flow grid. In the uncovered regions, the value from the uniform wind is left unaltered. The same is done in the case of the spiderweb file with operand 'O'. Regions for which data is missing in spatial fields are treated as non-existent in the file (currently no interpolation is by default active to fill gaps, therefore it is highly recommendable to complete these files in a preprocessing step). In netCDF files, missing data are recognized as values equal to the fill value designated in the

\_FillValue-attribute. In files for the Curvi-type (ASCII) it is the NODATA-value in the header.

A comprehensive list of keywords is given in the table below.

| quantity                | character | Name of the quantity, see the list below                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
|-------------------------|-----------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| filename                | character | File associated with this forcing                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| varname*                | character | Variable name used in filename associated with this forcing; some input files may contain multiple variables                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| sourcemask*             | character | File containing a mask                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| filetype                | integer   | Indication of the filetype: <ol> <li>1. Time series (C.4)</li> <li>2. Time series magnitude and direction</li> <li>3. Spatially varying weather</li> <li>4. ArcInfo</li> <li>5. Spiderweb data (cyclones) (C.14.3)</li> <li>6. Curvilinear data (C.14.2)</li> <li>7. Samples (C.3)</li> <li>8. Triangulation magnitude and direction</li> <li>9. Polyline (&lt;*.pli&gt;-file, C.2)</li> <li>11. NetCDF grid data (e.g. meteo fields)</li> <li>14. NetCDF wave data</li> </ol> |
| method                  | integer   | Method of interpolation: <ol> <li>1. Pass through (no interpolation)</li> <li>2. Interpolate time and space</li> <li>3. Interpolate time and space, save weights (+ optional extrapolation)</li> <li>4. Interpolate space</li> <li>5. Interpolate time</li> <li>7. Interpolate/Extrapolate time</li> </ol>                                                                                                                                                                     |
| extrapolation_method*   | integer   | Optionally allow nearest neighbour extrapolation in space (0: no, 1: yes). Default off.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| maxsearchradius*        | float     | Max search radius for nearest neighbor extrapolation in space.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| operand                 | character | Overwriting or superimposing values already set for this quantity: <ul> <li>'O' Values are overwritten.</li> <li>'+' New value is superimposed.</li> </ul>                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| value*                  | float     | custom coefficients for transformation                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| factor*                 | float     |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ifrctyp*                | float     |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| averagingtype*          | float     |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| relativesearchcellsize* | float     |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| extrapoltol*            | float     |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| area*                   | float     | Area for source/sink                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

**Note:** Keywords marked with \* are optional

![](_page_472_Picture_5.jpeg)

**Remark:**

- ◇ A polyline file specified as FILENAME for a boundary should only contain a single polyline. If you need boundaries that consist of multiple unconnected polylines, provide a separate block for each of them.

### C.6.3 New style external forcing

**Warning:**

- ◇ The new style external forcings file (ExtForceFileNew) is now the one and only place for various model forcings *and* spatial fields for initial conditions and model parameters.  
  As part of this migration, the [Meteo] block is deprecated and meteorological forcings will become part of the generic [Spatial] data fields.  
  See Section C.6.1 for a full description of the migration.

The name of this file is specified using the keyword ExtForceFileNew in the MDU-file (see Appendix A). Multiple external forcing files may be specified by separating the file names by a space. File names containing spaces must be enclosed in double quotes. External forcings are specified in the ini-file format. Table C.10 lists the structure of this file.

**Table C.10: Definition of external forcings.**

| Keyword                      | Type   | Default  | Description                     |
|------------------------------|--------|----------|---------------------------------|
| [General]                    |        |          |                                 |
| fileVersion                  | String | 3.00     | File version. Do not edit this. |
| fileType                     |        | extForce | File type. Do not edit this.    |
| [Boundary] definition(s)     |        |          | See Section C.6.3.1.            |
| [Lateral] definition(s)      |        |          | See Section C.6.3.2.            |
| [Meteo] definition(s)        |        |          | See Section C.6.3.3.            |
| [Spatial] definition(s)      |        |          | See Section C.6.3.4.            |
| [SourceSink] definition(s)   |        |          | See Section C.6.3.5.            |
| [BubbleScreen] definition(s) |        |          | See Section C.6.3.6.            |

This file may contain one or more [Boundary], [Lateral], [Meteo], [Spatial], [SourceSink] and [BubbleScreen] blocks, each followed by a set of keywords that specify the location and forcing or field data for that forcing. See the following sections for details.

**Example:**

```
[General]
fileVersion             = 3.00
fileType                = extForce[Boundary]
quantity               = waterlevelbnd
locationFile            = tfl_01.pli
forcingFile            = tfl_01.bc[Lateral]
id                     = Lateral1
name                    = First Lateral
locationType            = ld
branchId               = Channel1
chainage                = 250.000
discharge               = 27.3[Spatial]
quantity               = rainfall
dataFile               = precip.nc
dataFileType           = netcdf
targetMaskFile          = roofs.pol
targetMaskInvert       = yes
interpolationMethod = nearestNb[Spatial]
quantity              = frictionCoefficient
dataFile              = roughness.xyz
```

```
dataFileType                                = sample
interpolationMethod                         = triangulation[SourceSink]
id                                         = Id01
locationFile                                = sourcesink01.pliz
discharge                                    = discharge01.bc
```

### C.6.3.1 Boundary definitions

**Table C.11:** Boundary definitions in new style external forcing file.

| Keyword                                                            | Type   | Default  | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------|--------|----------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| <i>(Part of new-style external forcings file, see Table C.11.)</i> |        |          |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| [Boundary]                                                         |        |          | <i>Repeat as needed</i>                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| quantity                                                           | String |          | Name of the quantity, see the list in Section C.6.5 (boundaries only)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| locationFile                                                       | String |          | Name of boundary polyline <*.pli>.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| forcingFile                                                        | String |          | Name of file containing the forcing for this boundary. The file may either be a <bc> file (see Appendix C.5) or a netCDF-file (see section D.2.4).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| returnTime<br>(return_time in earlier versions)                    | Double | 0        | (Optional) Thatcher-Harleman return time [s]. See also section 4.3.4. The default value of 0 seconds means that the Thatcher-Harleman return time has no impact.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| tracerFallVelocity                                                 | Double | 0        | (Optional) Fall velocity for this tracer [m/s]. The default value 0 means that settling is disabled for this tracer.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| tracerDecayTime                                                    | Double | 0        | (Optional) Decay time $\tau$ for this tracer [s]. Specifies the timescale over which the tracer decays to approximately 36.8% (1/e) of its initial value. The default value 0 means that tracer decay is disabled for this tracer.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| operand                                                            | String | override | (optional) How this data is combined with previous data for the same quantity (if any). Supported operands: <ul style="list-style-type: none;"> <li>◇ override, override any previous data.</li> <li>◇ overrideIfMissing, sets only where data is still missing.</li> <li>◇ add, adds the provided values to the existing values.</li> <li>◇ multiply, multiplies the existing values by the provided values.</li> <li>◇ maximum, takes the maximum of the existing values and the provided values.</li> <li>◇ minimum, takes the minimum of the existing values and the provided values.</li> </ul> |

#### Remarks:

- ◇ The `tracerFallVelocity` is set *per tracer*, not per boundary location. Multiple boundaries for the same tracer should not specify different values, otherwise the first value is used. It is sufficient to set the `tracerFallVelocity` only once.
- ◇ The `tracerDecayTime` is also set *per tracer* and follows the same rules as in the previous remark.

- ◇ A polyline file specified as `locationFile` for a boundary should only contain a single polyline. If you need boundaries that consist of multiple unconnected polylines, provide a separate `[Boundary]+locationFile` for each of them.
- ◇ When multiple `[Boundary]` blocks are present with the same `quantity` name, the behavior depends on the `locationFile` name:
  - ◇ When also the `locationFile` full paths are the same, the boundaries are applied in the order in which they appear in the file, and are *added* on top of each other (comparable to implicitly setting `OPERAND=add`).
  - ◇ When the `locationFile` full paths are different, the boundaries are applied in the order in which they appear in the file, and are *overwriting* each other (comparable to implicitly setting `OPERAND=override`).
  - ◇ When using `<*.bc` files> the quantity names to be used in those files are described in Section C.5.3.

**Table C.12:** Lateral discharge definitions in new style external forcing file.

| Keyword                                                            | Type   | Default          | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------|--------|------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| <i>(Part of new-style external forcings file, see Table C.10.)</i> |        |                  |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| [Lateral]                                                          |        |                  | <i>Repeat as needed</i>                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

| <code>name</code>                                                  | String |                  | Long name in the user interface.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| <code>type</code>                                                  | String | <code>all</code> | <i>Deprecated.</i> Replaced by <code>locationType</code> .                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| <code>locationType</code>                                          | String | <code>all</code> | (optional) Only when <code>xCoordinates</code> and <code>yCoordinates</code> are also specified. Possible values are: <ul style="list-style-type: none;"> <li>◇ <code>1d</code>: only affect enclosed 1D grid points (only valid value when <code>nodeId</code> is given or <code>branchId</code> and chainage are given).</li> <li>◇ <code>2d</code>: only affect enclosed 2D grid points.</li> <li>◇ <code>all</code>: affect all enclosed grid points.</li> </ul>                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| <code>applyTransport</code>                                        | Int    | <code>0</code>   | (optional) Defines the way the concentrations of constituents at lateral locations are taken into account. <ul style="list-style-type: none;"> <li>◇ <code>0</code>: Only water (so without transport of constituents) is added to or removed from the model, depending on the sign of lateral discharge. For 3D models, lateral discharge is applied to the top layer of the model.</li> <li>◇ <code>1</code>: Transport of constituent is included. This option works only in combination with an external library via BMI-Interface. In a dimr configuration file, users can specify any constituents and layers of the lateral discharge. If the sign is positive, lateral discharge is passed to the model with a concentration set via the BMI-interface. When negative, discharge is passed from the model with a concentration equal to that of the ambient water in the model.</li> </ul> |
| <code>nodeId</code>                                                | String |                  | (optional) Node <code>id</code> of a 1D network node. The lateral will be connected to the grid point on/closest to that network node.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| <code>branchId</code>                                              | String |                  | (optional) For a 1D point lateral: branch on which the lateral discharge is located, in combination with chainage.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

| Keyword                               | Type     | Default | Description                                                                                                                 |
|---------------------------------------|----------|---------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| <i>(continued from previous page)</i> |          |         |                                                                                                                             |
| chainage                              | Double   |         | (optional) For a 1D point lateral: location on the branch of the point-lateral discharge [m], in combination with branchId. |
| numCoordinates                        | Int      |         | (optional) number of values in xCoordinates and yCoordinates. This value should be $\geq 1$ .                               |
| xCoordinates                          | Double[] |         | (optional) x-coordinates of the lateral discharge location polygon [m]. (number of values = numCoordinates).                |
| yCoordinates                          | Double[] |         | (optional) y-coordinates of the lateral discharge location polygon [m]. (number of values = numCoordinates).                |
| locationFile                          | String   |         | (optional) Name of lateral polygon <*.pol>.                                                                                 |
| discharge                             | *        |         | The prescribed discharge for this lateral [m <sup>3</sup> /s].                                                              |

- ◇ Three types of location specifications are available:
  - ◇ When `nodeId` is given, it will be used to snap the lateral to the grid point closest to that network node (only for 1D).
  - ◇ When `branchId` and `chainage` are given, they will be used for the location specification (only for 1D).
  - ◇ When `numCoordinates`, `xCoordinates` and `yCoordinates` are given, or when `locationFile` is given, the points will be used to define a polygon. When `numCoordinates ≥ 3`, the lateral discharge will be distributed over all grid points inside that polygon. When instead the number of polygon points = 1, only the 2D grid cell encompassing that single point will receive the full lateral discharge.
  - ◇ Items marked with (\*) can either be a scalar value, or a time series file (<\*.tim> (deprecated)/<\*.bc>) or realtime, to indicate that this parameter gets it values supplied by, e.g., realtime control.
  - ◇ When using <\*.bc files> the quantity names to be used in those files are described in [Section C.5.3](#).

**C.6.3.3 Meteorological forcings (deprecated)Warning:**

- ◇ The new style external forcings file (`ExtForceFileNew`) is now the one and only place for various model forcings *and* spatial fields for initial conditions and model parameters. As part of this migration, the `[Meteo]` is deprecated and meteorological forcings will become part of the generic `[Spatial]` data fields. See Section C.6.1 for a full description of the migration and Section C.6.3.4 for the `[Spatial]` block.

**C.6.3.4 Spatial data: meteorological forcings and various model input fieldsRemark:**

- ◇ The `[Spatial]` block supersedes both the deprecated `[Meteo]` block and the deprecated `IniFieldFile`. New schematizations should exclusively use `[Spatial]` blocks for spatially varying meteorological forcings, initial fields and model parameter fields.

The `[Spatial]` block is used to define spatially and/or time-varying input data. This includes both traditional meteorological forcing fields and various model input fields that were previously supplied through the `IniFieldFile`.

Examples of supported quantities include:

- ◇ Meteorological quantities such as wind, rainfall, heat-flux related quantities and stresses. Specific information for these quantities can be found in Chapter 15.
- ◇ Initial-condition quantities such as `initialWaterLevel` and `initialtracer`. Specific information for these quantities can be found in Appendix C.7.
- ◇ Spatial parameter quantities such as `frictionCoefficient`, `bedLevel`, and `horizontalEddyViscosityCoefficient`. Specific information for these quantities can be found in Appendix C.7.

Multiple `[Spatial]` blocks may be provided in a single external forcings file and also across multiple external forcings files. When multiple blocks define the same quantity, the order in which the blocks appear in the file(s) determines how they are combined through the `operand` setting.

- ◇ `dataFileType` = polygon should only be used for "vertical profile" quantities such as `initialVerticalSalinityProfile`. Formerly, another use was to set a constant value inside a polygon file. For that purpose provide a constant `dataValue` instead and list the polygon behind the `targetMaskFile`; do not use `dataFile` and `dataFileType` anymore.
- ◇ `dataFileType` = `ArcInfo` has two distinct uses:
  - ◇ Time-independent data on an equidistant 2D raster: official `ARC/INFO ASCII Grid` files<sup>1</sup>.
  - ◇ Time-varying data on an equidistant 2D raster: see [Section C.14.1](#).

Also see next remark regarding time-independent and time-varying data files in general:

- ◇ Time-independent data files are generally used for static parameters in the simulation, such as bedlevel or infiltration coefficient. Time-varying data files are not supported for these quantities. Time-varying data files are obviously suitable for all dynamic model parameters, such as meteorological forcings. Yet, it is also allowed to use time-independent data files for dynamic parameters, if time-constant forcing is desired.
- ◇ Friction coefficients may be provided of a different type than the model global type (i.e., MDU setting `UnifFrictCoef`). To do so, in addition to `quantity = friction` ←
  - Coefficient, add the extra keyword `frictionType` to the [Spatial] block. This is typically used on 2D grids. Spatially varying friction on 1D network is better prescribed using roughness files (??).

**C.6.4 File version history**Below are the most important file versions that have existed for the INI-based <\*.ext> file. File versions are formatted as <major>.<minor>. Major version changes indicate that older versions of the software are no longer readable. Minor version changes indicate that the software can still read the older (minor) file versions.

- ◇ 3.00: Generalization for the deprecation of both the old <\*.ext> file and the IniFieldFile. [Meteo] block generalized to [Spatial], made several keyword names consistent. operand values changed to more descriptive enumeration values.
- ◇ 2.03: Add [BubbleScreen] blocks.
- ◇ 2.02: Add [SourceSink] blocks.
- ◇ 2.01: New optional fields targetMaskFile and targetMaskInvert for [Meteo] blocks.
- ◇ 2.00: enabled specifying "nodeld" in a 1D network node for boundaries and lateral.
- ◇ 1.00: 1D2D distinction for laterals.
- ◇ Unversioned ("0.00"): First INI-formatted version of structures.ini for D-Flow FM. No [General] header and no network-specific input yet. Support for [Boundary], [Meteo] and [Lateral] blocks.

**C.6.5 Accepted quantity names**The list of accepted quantity names is subdivided into six categories:

- ◇ Boundary conditions (old and new <\*.ext> file)
- ◇ Meteorological fields (old and new <\*.ext> file)
- ◇ Structure parameters (old <\*.ext> file and Structure INI file)
- ◇ Initial fields (old <\*.ext> file and initial field/parameter file)
- ◇ Spatial physical properties (old <\*.ext> file and initial field/parameter file)
- ◇ Miscellaneous (mainly old <\*.ext> file)

## C.7 Initial conditions and spatially varying input

### C.7.1 Introduction

Spatially varying input is input data that varies in space such as initial conditions (water levels, etc.) or spatially varying model parameters (friction coefficients, etc.). D-Flow FM uses input data in *model-independent coordinates*, that is, the input files should contain their own spatial coordinates, and do not correspond with the D-Flow FM grid cell numbering. As a result, the model grid can always be changed, without the need to change all other spatial input. The spatial input will be interpolated onto the active model grid.

Initial conditions and spatial parameters used to be specified in a separate `IniFieldFile`, which is now deprecated. This input should now be placed under `[Spatial]` blocks. The generic file format and all available keywords are described in Section C.6.3.4. The following sections below contain more specific information regarding initial condition and parameter quantities, and which supported data file types are applicable.

#### Remark:

- ◇ Initial conditions can also be set using a restart-file, which assigns the exact values in the file to the current model grid. No interpolation is performed, and the restart file should correspond exactly with the current model. This is completely unrelated to the remainder of this chapter; please consult Section 8.8 instead.

This entire Appendix C.7 applies to both the deprecated and current functionality, except for the next subsection C.16.3, which only documents the deprecated `IniFieldFile` format and is kept for migration purposes only.

### C.7.2 IniFieldFile format for initial conditions and parameter fields (deprecated)

#### Warning:

- ◇ Deprecated: the initial and parameter fields file (`IniFieldFile`) is now deprecated. This will become obsolete in an upcoming release and the documentation below is only kept for migration purposes. Formerly, this data was specified in the old-style `<*.ext>-file`, which is now also deprecated.  
  See Section C.6.1 for a full description of the migration.

Initial and parameter fields are spatial fields that can describe initial conditions and spatially varying model parameters. The name of this file is specified using the keyword `IniFieldFile` in the MDU-file (see Appendix A). This file supersedes the old-style external forcings file for these quantities.

The fields are specified in the ini-file format. The order of blocks is relevant, since multiple data sets maybe combined for the same quantity (see operand in Table C.39). The order of keywords within a block is *not* relevant. Keywords and constants are case insensitive, but camel case is used as a naming convention. String values (e.g., filenames) are case sensitive.

This file may contain one or more **Initial** blocks or **Parameter** blocks, each followed by a set of keywords that specify the spatial data for that field. See the following table for details.

**Table C.20: Initial and parameter fields.**

| Keyword                     | Type   | Default  | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
|-----------------------------|--------|----------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [General]                   |        |          |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| fileVersion                 | String | 2.02     | File version. Do not edit this.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| fileType                    | String | iniField | File type. Do not edit this.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| <hr/>                       |        |          |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| [Initial] or<br>[Parameter] |        |          | <i>Repeat as needed</i>                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| quantity                    | String |          | Name of the quantity, see Table C.40 hereafter.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| dataFile                    | String |          | Name of file containing the field data values.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| dataFileType                | String |          | Type of dataFile. Supported types:<br>◇ ArcInfo<br>◇ GeoTIFF (section C.16.6.3)<br>◇ sample (Appendix C.3)<br>◇ netcdf (only valid for quantity = frictioncoefficient)<br>◇ polygon (Appendix C.2)<br><br>dataVariableName String (optional) Name of the variable in the data file, typically used for NetCDF input.<br><br>interpolationMethod String Type of (spatial) interpolation. Supported methods:<br><br>◇ constant, only with dataFileType=polygon.<br>◇ triangulation, Delaunay triangulation+linear interpolation, only supported for sample files.<br>◇ bilinear, bilinear interpolation, only supported for ArcInfo files.<br>◇ averaging, grid cell averaging.<br>◇ linearSpaceTime, linear interpolation in space and time (for time-dependent parameters)<br><br>operand String override (optional) How this data is combined with previous data for the same quantity (if any). Supported operands:<br><br>◇ O / override, override any previous data.<br>◇ A / overrideIfMissing, sets only where data is still missing.<br>◇ + / add, adds the provided values to the existing values.<br>◇ */multiply, multiplies the existing values by the provided values.<br>◇ X/maximum, takes the maximum of the existing values and the provided values.<br>◇ N/minimum, takes the minimum of the existing values and the provided values.<br><br><p style="text-align: right;"><i>(continued on next page)</i></p> |

|---------------------------------------|---------|---------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| <i>(continued from previous page)</i> |         |         |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| averagingType                         | String  | mean    | (optional) Type of averaging, if interpolationMethod=averaging. Supported types: <ul style="list-style-type: none;"> <li>◇ mean, arithmetic mean</li> <li>◇ nearestNb, nearest neighbour value</li> <li>◇ max, highest</li> <li>◇ min, lowest</li> <li>◇ invDist, inverse-distance-weighted average</li> <li>◇ minAbs, smallest absolute value</li> <li>◇ median, median value</li> </ul> |
| averagingRelSize                      | Double  | 1.01    | (optional) Relative search cell size for averaging.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| averagingNumMin                       | Integer | 1       | (optional) Minimum number of points in averaging. Must be $\geq 1$ .                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| averagingPercentile                   | Double  | 0.0     | (optional) Percentile value for which data values to include in averaging. 0.0 means off.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| extrapolationMethod                   | Logical | no      | Option for (spatial) extrapolation: no or yes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

Supported locations: <ul style="list-style-type: none;"> <li>◇ 1d, interpolate only to 1d nodes/links</li> <li>◇ 2d, interpolate only to 2d nodes/links</li> <li>◇ all, interpolate to all nodes/links</li> </ul>                                                                 |

The constant value to be set inside for all model points inside the polygon.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
